sections.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
sections.abstract: The paper proposes IB2, a protocol that evaluates enterprise AI by the complete serving route instead of an advertised model identifier.
sections.claimed_contribution: Gold-blind capability binding, reliability-inclusive scoring, and score-blind adjudication with released schemas and manifests.
sections.caveat: The sealed corpus and confounding from access mode, harness generation, and parsing limit direct comparability.

sections.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes
sections.abstract: A 955-case benchmark tests language models as transit-kiosk policy layers with structured tools and terminal states.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports held-out results for 26 models and releases the benchmark, harness, guide, and fine-tuned students.
sections.caveat: Results are benchmark- and serving-configuration-specific; most semantic components use a language-model judge.

sections.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
sections.abstract: SG-JEPA adds physics-parameter conditioning and multi-step latent rollout training for zero-shot generalization across gravitational fields.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports up to 2x lower open-loop error and up to 2.5x higher control success than DINO-WM on designed tasks.
sections.caveat: Transfer to real-world physics is not established by the reported abstract-level evidence.

sections.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
sections.abstract: FOM-UL selects layers with high forget-set influence and low retain-set sensitivity for targeted, quantization-resilient unlearning.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports lower residual memorization and preserved utility across several datasets and quantization settings.
sections.caveat: No formal erasure guarantee is claimed.

sections.title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
sections.abstract: Across nine evaluations, self-reports weakly predict model behavior and generic-agent prompts perform similarly.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports weak self-specific correlation and a flattering first-person bias.
sections.caveat: Generality depends on task, prompt, and behavioral-distribution choices.

sections.title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
sections.abstract: A post-release time-series hold-out shows that temporal freshness does not remove domain familiarity from pretraining.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports pretrained models winning 5 of 7 groups and a domain-familiarity association.
sections.caveat: Evidence covers 13 forecasters and seven groups.

sections.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls
sections.abstract: The paper compares fixed functional tokens with prompt-provided schemas for vehicle function calls in small language models.
sections.claimed_contribution: Schema-in-prompt generalizes to held-out functions and improves out-of-scope refusal, at memory and latency cost.
sections.caveat: Results are limited to single-turn vehicle function calling.

sections.title: EvalDetectBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Evaluation Awareness in Frontier Language Models
sections.abstract: EvalDetectBench measures whether frontier models recognize evaluation settings and whether benchmarks are detectable.
sections.claimed_contribution: Reports generator identity explaining 11.25% of measurement variance and proposes calibration and harmonisation.
sections.caveat: This is a prior-batch benchmark anchor, not a new 2026-09-10 submission.
